To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found significant spatial and temporal variability for traffic-related pollutants (particle-bound PAHs, ultrafine particles, PM2.5), with greater gradients for PAH and ultrafine concentrations than for PM2.5, and that the largest vehicles were most strongly associated with particle-bound PAH concentrations.
the concentrations of traffic-related pollutants were highest at roadside sites and that the concentrations of particle-bound PAHCs were significantly associated with diesel traffic.

the concentration of traffic-related pollutants in an urban area varies significantly with distance from the roadway and that the concentration gradient is steeper for some pollutants than for others.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of traffic on human health.
the health effects of air pollution in urban settings, particularly in the Boston area, which has some of the highest levels of particulate matter in the United States.
characterizing and modeling the spatial and temporal variability of traffic-related pollutants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data from this study suggest that traffic is a significant source of particle-bound PAHy and ultrafine particles, while diesel vehicles may be the primary source of these pollutants.
traffic-related air pollution is a major source of PAHs, ultrafine particles, PM2.5 and PM10 in urban centers.
the concentrations of PAH and ultrafine particles were higher at roadside locations and decreased with distance from the road, wind direction, and speed, and were associated with diesel vehicles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

traffic-related air pollution is a significant public health issue and that there is a need to better understand the spatial and temporal heterogeneities of these pollutants in order to develop more effective mitigation strategies.
the concentrations of traffic-related pollutants in an urban area are spatially and temporally heterogeneous and that the concentration gradients are different for different pollutants.

the data we collected are consistent with a traffic source for the pollutants we studied, and that the spatial and temporal variability of the concentrations of the pollutants we measured is likely to be a factor in any epidemiological study of traffic pollution and human health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concentrations and sources of traffic pollutants are highly heterogeneous, and that the concentrations are influenced by the meteorology.
traffic is a complex source of pollution and that the effects of traffic emissions are not uniform across the street or even within a single neighborhood.
the spatial and temporal heterogeneities in traffic-related pollutants are large, so that exposure assessment needs to be done with care.
